newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures climb on unemployment speculation.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures climb on unemployment speculation.

text.p: Bund futures advanced steadily on Wednesday as hopes built that Thursday's long-awaited German December employment report would show that the economy is weak.
Traders said the bond market was increasingly coming to the conclusion that Thursday's jobless data would show a rise of 60,000, above expectations of only a couple days earlier.
The speculation on unemployment, combined with stronger Treasuries, lifted the DTB Bund future 33 basis points in afternoon trade to 99.87, just off an earlier high of 99.92.
"Bond market fundamentals look very constructive for Bunds over the medium term," Bear Stearns wrote in a commentary.

Traders said recent comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer notwithstanding, they thought a strong rise in unemployment might prompt the Bundesbank to cut the repo rate in the first quarter of the year.
Although the Bundesbank meets tomorrow, all 10 economists surveyed by Reuters said they did not expect the central bank to make a move on interest rates on Thursday.

An auction for a new 10-year government Bund, meanwhile, appeared to go successfully with demand helped by lack of recent supply and a new feature that allows the debt to be stripped from its coupon from the middle of the year.

The German government sold 6.86 billion marks of the new 10-year bond bearing a six percent coupon at a lowest accepted price of 100.36. The average yield for the auction tranche was 5.94 percent. A five billion-mark first tranche was issued to the bond consortium on Tuesday.
A total of 15 billion marks of the new Bund is being placed, including the Bundesbank's share. Another 10 billion marks is due to be issued later in the month.
German gross domestic product data for 1996 will also be released on Thursday morning. A Reuter survey showed economists expected 1.4 percent growth.
Analysts said the GDP data, which is backward looking, will carry less market impact than the jobs figures.

The yield curve showed no sign of flattening on the day with the 2- to 10-year spread still around 242 basis points. Short maturity debt, however, had a difficult day with the two - to five-year spread narrowing two basis points to 141.
Bear Stearns wrote that government funding, which is favouring short maturity debt, should lead to a flatter yield curve over time.
Bunds were unable to keep pace with other European bond markets and underperformed.
Bunds slipped against French debt on speculation of a French rate cut and also underperformed against Treasuries.
U.S. debt was slightly stronger in late afternoon German trade.
